To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Nyquist-based analysis of stability is proposed for a positive feedback interconnected system with “mixed” properties.
the stability analysis for interconnected systems can be carried out by a classical Nyquist argument if the system is passive and has a negative imaginary part.

the stability of the positive feedback interconnection of two stable, linear, time-invariant systems, where one system has mixed passivity, negative imaginary, and small gain properties and the other has mixed negative imaginary, negative passivity, and small gain property, can be determined by the Nyquist plot of a certain transfer function.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the stability of positive feedback interconnection systems with “mixed" properties, where one subsystem has “mixed" passivity, negative imaginary and small-gain property and the other subsystem has “mixed” properties of negative passivity, negative imagi- nary and small gain.
the stability of positive feedback interconnections of linear systems.
the stability analysis of positive feedback interconnections between systems with mixed properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the interconnected systems are finite-gain stable if the following conditions hold: the Nyquist plots of the transfer functions G(s) and H(s) do not encircle the point (−1, j0) and the Nyquist plots are contained in the region |s| ≥ R, where R ≥ 0.
the proposed framework is an extension and generalization of the existing results for the finite-gain and robust stability analysis for interconnected systems.

the proposed framework is useful for stability analysis of interconnected systems with “mix” passivity, negativity-imaginary and/or small-gain properties, and the proposed framework is applicable in many practical systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed an analytical framework to examine stability for a positive-feedback interconnection between two linear time-invariant (LTI) systems.

we have proposed an analytical framework for the finite-gain L2 stability of positive feedback interconnected systems where one system is passive with respect to one input and one output, negative imaginary with respect to the remaining input-output pair, and small gain, and the other system is negative imaginary with respect two inputs and one output, positive with respect to the other output, and small gain.
we propose a framework to examine the stability for interconnected systems with mixed passivity, negative imaginary and small gain properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, if one can prove that the interconnected system is stable, the stability of the system can be certified by a single Nyquist plot.
the proposed framework provides a simple way to examine the finite gain stability of interconnected systems where one system is passivity based and the other system is negative-imaginary based.
, in general, the stability of interconnected systems cannot be determined using only the passivity, negative imaginary, and small-gains properties of each subsystem.
